method: Every allegation and every piece of claimed corroboration in the public record, with the reporter's own words on provenance. Class labels describe what reporters SAID they had; they are not a ruling on whether any allegation is true. 'Independently verified' means examined by an investigation independent of the outlet that published the story (law enforcement, court process, or a disinterested third-party review) — not the outlet's own account of its reporting. No charge, court finding, or adjudication exists anywhere in this record.

classes.EXAMINED: Reporter says they personally saw the document/item
classes.RELAYED: Described to the reporter but not examined
classes.OUTCRY: Third party recounting what the accuser told them at the time
classes.METHOD: The reporting process itself offered as corroboration
classes.ABSENT: No record exists or none was produced
classes.NOT-CORROBORATED: The outlet itself said it could not corroborate
classes.NON-DENIAL: The campaign did not dispute the specific item
classes.CHECKED-NEGATIVE: The outlet checked and found no evidence
classes.DOCUMENTED: Figure or fact confirmed on the record by a named party

allegations.claim: Alleges that in late 2021 Platner entered her home uninvited while deeply intoxicated and forced himself on her as she repeatedly told him to stop.
allegations.denial: “Any accusation of non-consensual behavior is categorically untrue.” — Platner

items.provenance: “There is no police report in this case.” — Adam Wren, on air (MS NOW / Morning Joe, Jul 7, 2026)
items.establishes: No official or legal record exists; the gap the other items were marshaled to fill.

items.provenance: “We reviewed email exchanges between she and her therapist, referring to what she called this sexual assault and her therapist sort of acknowledging that this had happened to her.” — Wren, on air. In print, per Politico's own description (as read on air, Breaking Points, Jul 8, 2026): “Racicot showed POLITICO recent emails with her therapist” in which she explained she was talking to the media; “Her therapist responded that Racicot shouldn't have to speak publicly about a traumatic incident in order to be believed, without referencing details of any particular incident.” The therapist declined to comment.
items.establishes: Her discussion of the allegation with her therapist — not independent proof of the act. Emails were produced by Racicot. CORRECTED 2026-07-12: this entry previously read the emails as contemporaneous with the event; Politico's printed description dates them to June 2026, during her conversations with reporters — the on-air characterization was “in almost real time.”

items.provenance: “We talked to people who she had spoken with contemporaneously about these attacks and all of those stories lined up and checked out.” — Wren, on air
items.establishes: Their accounts of what she told them at the time were consistent, per the reporter.

items.item: Screenshots of her messages to others (“consensually careless”)
items.provenance: “We saw screenshots that she shared of messages relaying this account to others” … “long before he was … a political candidate.” — Wren, on air
items.establishes: She relayed the account to third parties before his candidacy; bears on timing/motive.

items.provenance: “She tried to recover those DMs. We were not able to review those DMs, but she described them to us.” — Wren, on air
items.establishes: The direct exchange between the two people was never reviewed by the reporters — stated plainly, twice, under questioning.

items.provenance: “One night in November or December of 2021, she said she texted him to say that she could use a massage. She said she did not intend it as an invitation, but he interpreted it that way, immediately replying to say he would come right over. She said she wrote back twice, telling him not to. The Post was not able to review the alleged messages or independently verify them. Racicot said she later deleted them soon after the incident.” — The Washington Post, Jul 6, 2026. Politico's story said she “told him not to come over” and described him as “uninvited,” without the preceding message; a Politico reporter's message to the Platner campaign — obtained and authenticated by Ryan Grim (Breaking Points / Drop Site, Jul 8, 2026) — reads: “texting Platner about needing her glute massaged. That detail didn't make our story.” Politico, in response: “This story is based on extensive reporting and interviews and reflects our editorial standards… If presented with information that materially challenges our reporting, we will report it.”
items.establishes: The texts preceding his arrival were deleted (per her account) and never reviewed by any outlet. She volunteered the detail to multiple outlets — Grim: it “strengthens the credibility of her version of events” — one outlet printed a version of it; the outlet of record did not.

items.provenance: “We interviewed her … three separate times. Her story stayed consistent across those times.” — Wren, on air
items.establishes: Internal consistency across repeated interviews with the same outlet.

items.item: Racicot in the NYT, June 4 — same episode, no assault allegation
items.provenance: “She declined to elaborate, but said she cut off contact soon after that episode and found his behavior ‘reckless’ and ‘unsettling.’” — NYT, Jun 4, 2026
items.establishes: The assault allegation is a Politico artifact; the NYT had the same person on record a month earlier without it.

allegations.claim: Alleges that while they dated (~2013–2015) Platner grabbed her hard enough to leave marks and once physically restrained her during an argument.
allegations.outlet_of_record: The New York Times, June 4, 2026 (Katie Glueck, Lisa Lerer)
allegations.denial: Platner “strongly disputes” any claims of physical intimidation or altercations (campaign).

items.provenance: “The Times could not independently corroborate Ms. Fifield's account of the altercations.” — NYT, in print
items.establishes: The publishing outlet itself states the physical claims were not independently corroborated.

items.provenance: “…confirmed that the pair had an emotionally volatile relationship but could not corroborate the physical altercations or the most controversial comments she described.” — NYT
items.establishes: Volatility corroborated; the physical altercations and most controversial comments were not. By her own account she told no one at the time.

items.provenance: “The Times reviewed texts between Ms. Fifield and Mr. Platner, along with Google Chat exchanges, texts and Facebook messages between Ms. Fifield and her friends during and after the relationship.”
items.establishes: The relationship's existence and tenor — not the disputed incidents.

items.provenance: “The Times also reviewed some of Ms. Fifield's diary entries from after the relationship had ended.”
items.establishes: Post-relationship state of mind — the entries are not contemporaneous with the alleged incidents.

allegations.claim: Alleges Platner knew years ago that his chest tattoo was a Nazi symbol and called it “my Totenkopf” — contradicting his account that he learned of the association from reporters in 2025.
allegations.outlet_of_record: NYT June 4, 2026; CNN June 5, 2026; Jewish Insider Oct 21, 2025 (separate acquaintance)
allegations.denial: Platner “strongly disputes” her account of what he knew and what he told her (campaign).

items.item: Aug. 20, 2025 group-chat screenshot (“It's a Totenkopf … An actual one”)
items.provenance: “…months before Mr. Platner acknowledged the tattoo himself … according to a screenshot she shared with The Times.” — NYT
items.establishes: Her strongest dated document: it proves SHE said it before the controversy — not that HE told her. The underlying ‘he knew’ claim remains her word against his denial.

items.item: Photo of the tattoo in her possession
items.provenance: “I had no photographic evidence of it … if I'm fabricating this story, I'm doing it without even having a photo of this tattoo.” — Fifield, on camera (CNN interview, Jul 7, 2026)
items.establishes: She had no photo; her early claims were made without documentary imagery.

items.item: “My Totenkopf” at a Capitol Hill bar (~2012)
items.provenance: A former acquaintance said Platner referred to it as “my Totenkopf” at a Capitol Hill bar around 2012. — Jewish Insider, Oct 21, 2025
items.establishes: A second person making a parallel claim; anonymous in the original CNN piece, one corroborating person per CNN Oct 24.

allegations.claim: Recalls Platner repeatedly saying that if anybody broke in, “I would rape them … to show them that I'm dominant.”
allegations.denial: None on this item — see provenance.

items.provenance: “Asked about those remarks, a Platner campaign official did not dispute them. A friend who knew Mr. Platner and Ms. Fifield during that period said the comments sounded out of character.” — NYT
items.establishes: The campaign's non-denial is the closest thing to corroboration on this item, per the article's own framing.

allegations.claim: Alleges Platner removed condoms during sex without her consent (reported as allegedly at least six times).
allegations.outlet_of_record: The Washington Post, July 7, 2026; CNN, July 7, 2026 — [secondary: WaPo not read in full in this archive]
allegations.denial: Campaign called the July allegations “categorically false,” from “a person with a well-documented political agenda.”

items.provenance: [Secondary] A friend told the Post she recalled Fifield being upset at the time; CNN's piece reported a friend (Emily Zanotti) saying Fifield described it years earlier.
items.establishes: Contemporaneous complaint recalled by a friend; otherwise her account. She said she had shared it off the record with the NYT earlier but was too embarrassed to go public until after the Racicot story.

context_checks.provenance: “Records show no evidence of any relationship between Ms. Fifield and the Collins campaign.” — NYT
context_checks.establishes: The NYT checked for a coordination tie and found none.

context_checks.provenance: Roughly $15,000 total over 2021–2022; never an employee; last paid 2022 — per IW president Carrie Lukas, in the NYT.
context_checks.establishes: The documented money trail between Fifield and the conservative organization.

context_checks.provenance: CNN (Jul 7) identified activist/lawyer Cheyenne Hunt as having connected accusers with media; CJR (Jul 8, Betsy Morais) examined that role in detail.
context_checks.establishes: How the accusers reached reporters — documented by the outlets themselves and by a journalism-review analysis.
